mainTopic: קידוש החודש by בית דין: רבן גמליאל's acceptance of doubtful witnesses, the clash with רבי יהושע, and the binding authority of every generation's court
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about witnesses for קידוש החודש. In two cases רבן גמליאל accepts witnesses whom other חכמים call עדי שקר. In the second case רבי יהושע sides with רבי דוסא בן הורכינס, so רבן גמליאל orders him to come with his staff and money on the day רבי יהושע counts as יום הכפורים. רבי עקיבא and רבי דוסא convince him that the בית דין's dates stand, and רבן גמליאל greets him as 'my teacher and my student'. The גמרא then explains רבן גמליאל's family tradition that the moon's path is sometimes long and sometimes short. It also tells stories about the moon's timing: רבי חייא and the old moon, and רבן גמליאל blocking a ראש חודש declared on the 29th. Finally it expands on רבי עקיבא's teaching that אֹתָם can be read as אַתֶּם, and on why the seventy elders are not named: every generation's בית דין carries full authority.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי calls the first witnesses liars
steps.stepSummary: The witnesses finish their testimony: they saw the moon in the evening in the west. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says they must be lying.
steps.simpleTranslation: The witnesses said they also saw the moon in the evening in the west. רבי יוחנן בן נורי said: they are false witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the witnesses' strange testimony, and רבי יוחנן בן נורי rejects it as impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses claimed they saw the old moon in the morning and the new moon that same evening. That cannot happen on the same day, so רבי יוחנן בן נורי says the testimony is false.

keyTerms.meaning: The west, where the new moon appears after sunset

phrases.english: and in the evening in the west.
Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said:
They are false witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי עֵדֵי שֶׁקֶר הֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the testimony begun earlier in the משנה and gives the first reaction to it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Testimony that the moon was seen in the morning in the east and the same evening in the west is false.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל accepts them anyway
steps.stepSummary: When the same witnesses came to יבנה, רבן גמליאל accepted their testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they came to יבנה, רבן גמליאל accepted them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us that רבן גמליאל, the head of the בית דין, did accept these witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the main tension of the passage. A great חכם called the witnesses liars, but the head of the בית דין accepted them and set the month by their testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: The town where the great בית דין sat after the Temple was destroyed

phrases.english: When they came to Yavne,
Rabban Gamliel accepted them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁבָּאוּ לְיַבְנֶה קִיבְּלָן רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual ruling of בית דין, which goes against רבי יוחנן בן נורי's rejection.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל accepted the witnesses despite the objection.

steps.title: A second case: seen on time, but not the next night
steps.stepSummary: Two witnesses said they saw the new moon at its expected time, but the next night it was not seen. רבן גמליאל accepted them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another case: two witnesses came and said, 'We saw it at its time,' but on the next night it was not seen. And רבן גמליאל accepted them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a second story where רבן גמליאל accepted witnesses whose claim looked doubtful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the moon really appeared on the 30th night, it should be even easier to see on the 31st. Even so, nobody saw it the next night, but רבן גמליאל still set ראש חודש on the 30th based on the witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: At its time, on the night of the 30th day
The next night, which would make the old month full (30 days)

phrases.english: And another time, two came and said:
We saw it at its time,
and on the night of its extension it was not seen,
phrases.notes: This means the following night, which would have made the old month 30 days long.

phrases.english: and Rabban Gamliel accepted them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד בָּאוּ שְׁנַיִם וְאָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, similar case where רבן גמליאל accepted doubtful witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל accepted witnesses who saw the moon on the 30th even though it was not seen on the 31st.

steps.title: רבי דוסא: like a woman who gave birth but is still pregnant
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא בן הורכינס says these witnesses are false and uses a sharp comparison to show their claim cannot be true.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא בן הורכינס said: They are false witnesses. How can people testify that a woman gave birth, when the next day her belly is still out to her teeth?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסא challenges רבן גמליאל's acceptance in the second case by showing the claim is self-contradicting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the moon was visible one night and invisible the next is like saying a woman gave birth yesterday but is clearly still pregnant today. The second fact proves the first one false. So he holds the month should have been made full, with ראש חודש a day later.

keyTerms.meaning: Between her teeth, a picture of a big pregnant belly

steps.confusionAlert: רבי דוסא is not talking about a real woman. The birth story is only a comparison to show how the witnesses contradict themselves.

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa ben Horkinas said:
They are false witnesses;
how can they testify about a woman that she gave birth,
and the next day her belly is between her teeth?

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵדֵי שֶׁקֶר הֵן הֵיאַךְ מְעִידִים עַל הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיָּלְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבן גמליאל's acceptance of the witnesses in the second case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's acceptance of witnesses who saw the moon on the 30th when it was not seen on the 31st.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A moon seen one night must be visible the next night. Its absence proves the earlier sighting false, just as a woman who is still pregnant could not have given birth the day before.

steps.title: רבי יהושע agrees with Rabbi Dosa
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע tells רבי דוסא that he accepts his reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: I see your point.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע publicly sides with רבי דוסא against רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now a leading חכם agrees that the month was set on the wrong day. This means יום הכפורים would fall a day later by רבי יהושע's count than by רבן גמליאל's count. That sets up the conflict in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
I see your words.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ רוֹאֶה אֲנִי אֶת דְּבָרֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי דוסא's challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע agrees that the witnesses were false and that the month should have been made full.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's decree: come with your staff and money
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל orders רבי יהושע to come to him carrying his staff and money on the day that falls on יום הכפורים by רבי יהושע's count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל sent to him: I decree that you come to me with your staff and your money on the day that is יום הכפורים according to your calculation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל responds to the challenge with an order that makes רבי יהושע act as if his own calculation is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying a staff and money is forbidden on יום הכפורים. By forcing רבי יהושע to do this on 'his' יום הכפורים, רבן גמליאל makes it clear that only the בית דין's date counts.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the authority of the head of the בית דין in setting the calendar is binding on everyone, even on a great חכם who disagrees.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel sent to him:
I decree upon you that you come to me
with your staff and with your money
on Yom Kippur
that falls according to your calculation.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁלַח לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל גּוֹזְרַנִי עָלֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבן גמליאל responds to רבי יהושע's agreement with רבי דוסא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע must treat the day by his own count as an ordinary weekday, following the בית דין's date.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's proof that בית דין's dates stand
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא finds רבי יהושע upset and proves from a פסוק that whatever רבן גמליאל set is valid, even if it was not at the right time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא went and found him distressed. He said: I can learn that whatever רבן גמליאל did is done, as it says, 'These are the appointed times of ה׳, holy gatherings, that you shall proclaim.' Whether at their right time or not, I have no festivals except these.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא comforts רבי יהושע by bringing a פסוק that shows the בית דין's declaration decides when the festivals are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the festivals are the ones 'that you shall proclaim'. So the festivals depend on בית דין's proclamation, not only on the true astronomy. That means רבי יהושע is not actually breaking יום הכפורים by obeying.
steps.whatToRemember: The calendar follows the declaration of בית דין. Once they set the month, the festivals fall by that date, even if the setting was mistaken.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source for the idea that the authority to set the Jewish calendar rests with בית דין's proclamation.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva went and found him distressed,
he said to him: I can learn

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכׇּל מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל עָשׂוּי,
phrases.english: that everything Rabban Gamliel did is done,
as it is said:
"These are the appointed times of the Lord, holy gatherings,
which you shall proclaim them" —
whether at their time or not at their time,
I have no festivals other than these.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ לִי לִלְמוֹד שֶׁכׇּל מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל עָשׂוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem created by רבן גמליאל's decree by showing that obeying it is correct.
steps.raayaObject: That every date set by רבן גמליאל, as head of בית דין, is binding.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 23:4, 'אשר תקראו אתם', which makes the festivals depend on בית דין's proclamation, whether at the right time or not.

steps.title: רבי דוסא says we cannot question every court
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא בן הורכינס tells רבי יהושע that if we question רבן גמליאל's court, we would have to question every court since משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע came to רבי דוסא בן הורכינס. רבי דוסא said to him: If we start questioning the rulings of רבן גמליאל's court, we would have to question every single court that has stood from the days of משה until now.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע visits רבי דוסא, who argues that a בית דין's ruling must be accepted. This sets up the proof from a פסוק that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי דוסא himself said the witnesses were false. Now he says that even so, we may not overturn the court's ruling. If every ruling could be reopened, no court's decisions would ever stand.

keyTerms.meaning: to question or re-judge after someone

steps.confusionAlert: רבי דוסא is not changing his mind about the witnesses. He still thinks they were wrong. He is saying that the court's decision binds everyone anyway.

phrases.aramaic: בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל רַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הוֹרְכִּינָס,
phrases.english: He (רבי יהושע) came to Rabbi Dosa ben Horkinas,
he said to him:
phrases.notes: Here רבי דוסא is the one speaking to רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: If we come to question

phrases.aramaic: אַחַר בֵּית דִּינוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: the rulings of the court of Rabban Gamliel,
we must also question

phrases.aramaic: אַחַר כׇּל בֵּית דִּין וּבֵית דִּין
phrases.english: the rulings of each and every court
that has stood from the days of Moshe until now.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל רַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הוֹרְכִּינָס, אָמַר לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי עקיבא's proof, רבי יהושע goes to רבי דוסא, who adds another argument for accepting the ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rulings of an official בית דין cannot be reopened. Otherwise every court in history would be open to question.

steps.title: The unnamed elders show every court is like משה's
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא proves from the unnamed seventy elders that every court of three is like משה's court.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Then משה went up with אהרן, נדב, אביהוא, and seventy of the elders of ישראל.' Why does the פסוק not tell us the names of the elders? To teach that any group of three that serves as a בית דין over ישראל is like the court of משה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסא backs up his claim with a פסוק. He learns something from the fact that the elders' names are missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The elders are not named, so their greatness as individuals is not what counts. What counts is that they served as the official court. In the same way, any properly appointed court has the authority of משה's court.

keyTerms.meaning: their names were not spelled out

steps.whatToRemember: A properly appointed court has full authority, even if its judges are not as great as משה. So רבי יהושע must accept רבן גמליאל's ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main reason Jewish law follows the official בית דין of each generation, even when other scholars disagree.

phrases.english: As it is said:
"Then Moshe went up, and Aharon, Nadav and Avihu,
and seventy of the elders of Israel."

phrases.aramaic: וְלָמָּה לֹא נִתְפָּרְשׁוּ שְׁמוֹתָן שֶׁל זְקֵנִים?
phrases.english: And why were the names of the elders not spelled out?
Rather, it is to teach that every group of three
that stood as a court over Israel

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא כְּבֵית דִּינוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה.
phrases.english: is like the court of Moshe.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיַּעַל מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן נָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim made in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: Every official court has the authority of משה's court.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 24:9: the seventy elders are not named.

steps.title: רבי יהושע goes to יבנה on his own יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע obeys and travels to רבן גמליאל with his staff and money on his own count's יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע took his staff and his money in his hand. He went to יבנה, to רבן גמליאל, on the day that was יום הכפורים according to his own calculation.
steps.whatsHappening: Convinced by רבי עקיבא and רבי דוסא, רבי יהושע does exactly what רבן גמליאל ordered in Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By carrying a staff and money and traveling, he openly treats that day as a regular weekday. This shows he fully accepts the court's calendar over his own opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: the town where רבן גמליאל's court sat

phrases.english: He took his staff and his money in his hand,
and went to Yavneh, to Rabban Gamliel,
on the day on which Yom Kippur fell
according to his own calculation.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָטַל מַקְלוֹ וּמְעוֹתָיו בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהושע acts on the arguments of Steps 7 to 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע submits to רבן גמליאל's order in action.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל greets him as teacher and student
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל kisses רבי יהושע and calls him 'my teacher and my student'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל stood up and kissed him on his head. He said to him: Come in peace, my teacher and my student! My teacher in wisdom, and my student because you accepted my words.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with peace. רבן גמליאל honors רבי יהושע for his wisdom and for accepting the court's authority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The title 'teacher' admits that רבי יהושע was greater in wisdom. The title 'student' praises him for giving in. Being greater in wisdom does not cancel the court's authority.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's story teaches that even a greater scholar must follow the official בית דין. Doing so brings honor and peace.

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וּנְשָׁקוֹ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel stood up and kissed him on his head,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: בּוֹא בְּשָׁלוֹם רַבִּי וְתַלְמִידִי!
phrases.english: he said to him: Come in peace, my teacher and my student!
My teacher in wisdom,
and my student, because you accepted my words.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמַד רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וּנְשָׁקוֹ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story begun when רבי יהושע obeyed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute ends with honor on both sides. The court's authority is upheld, and רבי יהושע's wisdom is still respected.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's family tradition about the moon
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא: רבן גמליאל had a tradition that the moon's path is sometimes long and sometimes short.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבן גמליאל said to the חכמים: This is what I received from my grandfather's house. Sometimes the moon comes by a long path, and sometimes by a short one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now begins. It brings רבן גמליאל's tradition to explain why he accepted the first witnesses (Steps 1–2), who saw the old moon in the morning and the new moon that same evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said it is impossible to see the old moon in the morning and the new moon that same evening. רבן גמליאל answers that the moon's path is not always the same length, so sometimes the new moon appears very soon after the old one. That means the witnesses are not automatically false.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Long' and 'short' are about how much time the moon takes in its monthly cycle. This is why it can sometimes be seen earlier or later than expected.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught (in a ברייתא):
Rabban Gamliel said to the Sages:
This is what I received from the house of my father's father:
sometimes it comes by a long path
phrases.notes: 'It' is the moon, which the ברייתא doesn't name but assumes.

phrases.english: and sometimes it comes by a short path.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר לָהֶם רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לַחֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first case (Steps 1–2) and explains רבן גמליאל's reasoning against רבי יוחנן בן נורי's claim that the witnesses were false.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The moon's path is not fixed. So the new moon can sometimes appear very soon after the old moon was last seen.

steps.title: A verse shows the moon has no fixed schedule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן supports the tradition of רבן גמליאל's family from a פסוק: the sun knows its setting, but the moon does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: What is the reason of the house of רבי? Because it is written: 'He made the moon for the seasons; the sun knows its setting.' It is the sun that knows its setting. The moon does not know its setting.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a source in the פסוק for רבן גמליאל's family tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says only about the sun that it 'knows its setting'. This hints that the moon does not keep a fixed schedule. That supports the claim that the moon's path is sometimes long and sometimes short.

keyTerms.meaning: the house of רבי (the family of the נשיא)
knows its setting (keeps a fixed schedule)

steps.whatToRemember: The sun's cycle is fixed, but the moon's is not. This backs רבן גמליאל's acceptance of the witnesses.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is the reason of the house of Rabbi?
phrases.notes: This means the family of the נשיא, where רבן גמליאל's tradition came from.

phrases.english: As it is written: "He made the moon for seasons;
the sun knows its setting"
it is the sun that knows its setting,
the moon does not know its setting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for the tradition in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The moon's cycle varies, unlike the sun's.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 104:19: only the sun is described as knowing its setting.

steps.title: רבי חייא scolds the old moon
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא sees the old moon still showing on the morning of the 29th. He throws a clod of earth at it and tells it to go hide, because the new moon must be seen tonight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא saw the moon still standing in the sky on the morning of the 29th of the month. He took a clump of earth, threw it at the moon and said: Tonight we need to sanctify you, and you are still standing here?! Go cover yourself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that ties in with רבן גמליאל's tradition that the moon's path is sometimes long and sometimes short.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the old moon can still be seen on the morning of the 29th, it seems too early for the new moon to appear that same night. רבי חייא is worried this will block declaring ראש חודש on the 30th. His throwing the clod is a dramatic way of showing that worry.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya saw the moon
that was standing in the sky on the morning of the twenty-ninth.
He took a clump of earth and threw it at it,
he said: Tonight we need to sanctify you,
and you are still standing here?!
Go, cover yourself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא חַזְיֵיא לְסֵיהֲרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story about the moon's timing after the פסוק that the moon does not know its setting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing the old moon on the morning of the 29th made it seem the new moon could not appear that night.

steps.title: רבי sends רבי חייא to sanctify the month in עין טב
steps.stepSummary: רבי tells רבי חייא to go to עין טב, sanctify the month there, and send back the coded sign 'דוד מלך ישראל חי וקים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said to רבי חייא: Go to עין טב and sanctify the month, and send me a sign: 'דוד מלך ישראל חי וקים' (דוד, king of ישראל, lives and endures).
steps.whatsHappening: Another short story about קידוש החודש: רבי sends רבי חייא to a place called עין טב to sanctify the month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sanctifying is done in עין טב and not where רבי is. רבי asks for a set phrase as a sign, so he will know the month was sanctified.

keyTerms.meaning: A place name where the month was sanctified

phrases.english: Rabbi said to Rabbi Chiya:
Go to Ein Tav and sanctify the month,
and send me a sign:
"David, king of Israel, lives and endures."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about רבי חייא and the new month.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי sent רבי חייא to sanctify the month in עין טב and to report back with a coded phrase.

steps.title: The court wants to declare ראש חודש on the 29th
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: on a cloudy day, something that looked like the moon was seen on the 29th. The people thought it was ראש חודש, and the court wanted to sanctify it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Once the sky was covered with clouds, and the form of the moon was seen on the 29th of the month. The people thought it was ראש חודש, and the court wanted to sanctify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that sets up a problem. רבן גמליאל will respond to it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sky was cloudy, so what people saw only looked like the moon. That was enough to make the people and the court want to declare ראש חודש on the 29th.

keyTerms.meaning: The form, the look, of the moon

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Once
the sky was covered with clouds,
and the form of the moon was seen
on the twenty-ninth of the month.
The people thought to say it was Rosh Chodesh,
and the court wanted to sanctify it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פַּעַם אַחַת נִתְקַשְּׁרוּ שָׁמַיִם בְּעָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא about seeing the moon on the 29th, like רבי חייא's story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Something like the moon was seen on a cloudy 29th, and the court wanted to declare ראש חודש.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's family tradition on the moon's cycle
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל stops the court. He has a family tradition that the moon's cycle is never shorter than 29½ days, ⅔ of an hour and 73 parts. So the new moon could not appear on the 29th.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to them: This is what I received from my grandfather's house. The renewal of the moon is not less than 29½ days, plus two-thirds of an hour, plus 73 parts.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל pushes back against the court's plan. He shows from his family tradition that the moon could not really have been seen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new moon cannot come before at least 29½ days and a bit more. So on the 29th it is too early, and what the people saw cannot have been the new moon.

keyTerms.meaning: The renewal of the moon, the moon's cycle
Parts, small units of an hour

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the exact length of the moon's cycle that the Jewish calendar is based on.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to them:
This is what I received from my father's father's house:
the renewal of the moon is not
less than twenty-nine and a half days
and two-thirds of an hour
and seventy-three parts.
phrases.notes: Here an hour is split into 1,080 small parts, so 73 parts is a few minutes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: כָּךְ מְקוּבְּלַנִי מִבֵּית אֲבִי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the court's plan from step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The plan to declare ראש חודש on the 29th
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The moon's cycle is never shorter than 29½ days plus a little, so the new moon cannot be seen on the 29th.

steps.title: A הספד to show it was not ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: That day the mother of בן זזא died. רבן גמליאל gave her a big eulogy, not because she deserved it, but so the people would know the court had not declared ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: On that day the mother of בן זזא died, and רבן גמליאל gave her a great eulogy. He did it not because she was worthy of it, but so the people would know that the court had not sanctified the month.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends the story by showing how רבן גמליאל let everyone know that the day was not ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A big public eulogy is not given on ראש חודש. By giving one, רבן גמליאל showed everyone, without a speech, that the day was a regular day.

keyTerms.meaning: A Sage whose mother died that day

steps.whatToRemember: רבן גמליאל did not let a cloudy sighting change the calendar, and he made sure the public knew it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם מֵתָה אִמּוֹ שֶׁל בֶּן זָזָא,
phrases.english: And on that day the mother of Ben Zaza died,
and Rabban Gamliel gave her a great eulogy.
Not because she was worthy of it,
but so that the people would know

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא קִידְּשׁוּ בֵּית דִּין אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: that the court had not sanctified the month.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם מֵתָה אִמּוֹ שֶׁל בֶּן זָזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא by showing the public result of רבן גמליאל's decision.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The court did not sanctify the month, and the eulogy made that public.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי עקיבא found him upset
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: 'רבי עקיבא went and found him upset.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא went and found him upset, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה. This step sets up a question about that line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words in the משנה are unclear: 'found him upset' could mean רבי עקיבא was upset when he found רבי יהושע, or that רבי יהושע was the one who was upset. The next step asks exactly this.

phrases.aramaic: הָלַךְ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וּמְצָאוֹ מֵיצֵר כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva went and found him upset, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלַךְ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וּמְצָאוֹ מֵיצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the moon stories and goes back to the story of רבי יהושע in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה says רבי עקיבא went and found him upset.

steps.title: Who was upset?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: in the משנה, was רבי עקיבא the one who was upset, or רבי יהושע?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Who was upset? Was רבי עקיבא upset, or was רבי יהושע upset?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to understand who the word 'upset' in the משנה refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sentence can be read two ways. The question is about the meaning of the משנה's words, not about the law.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked, a question was raised

phrases.english: They asked: Who was upset?
Was Rabbi Akiva upset,
or was Rabbi Yehoshua upset?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מִי מֵיצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the unclear wording quoted in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the word 'upset' in the משנה refers to רבי עקיבא or to רבי יהושע.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהושע was upset
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says clearly: רבי עקיבא found רבי יהושע upset and asked him why.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it was taught: רבי עקיבא went and found רבי יהושע while he was upset. He said to him: My teacher, why are you upset?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא that names רבי יהושע as the one who was upset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spells out the name the משנה left out. רבי עקיבא asks the question, so he is the visitor and רבי יהושע is the one who is upset.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: הָלַךְ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וּמְצָאוֹ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva went and found Rabbi Yehoshua
while he was upset,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: [רַבִּי] מִפְּנֵי מָה אַתָּה מֵיצֵר?
phrases.english: he said to him: [My teacher,] why are you upset?
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא: הָלַךְ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וּמְצָאוֹ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע was the one who was upset, as the ברייתא says.

steps.title: Better to be sick for a year than face this decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers רבי עקיבא: it would be better for a person to be sick in bed for twelve months than to have this decree put on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי עקיבא, it is better for a person to fall sick in bed for twelve months than to have this decree made against him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע explains why he is upset. This closes the answer: he was deeply pained by רבן גמליאל's order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע was ordered to travel on the day that he counted as יום הכפורים. He says a year of sickness would be easier than this, which shows how hard the order was for him.
steps.whatToRemember: The one who was upset was רבי יהושע. He felt רבן גמליאל's order to break his own count's יום הכפורים was worse than a year of sickness.

phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: רָאוּי לוֹ שֶׁיִּפּוֹל לַמִּטָּה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: it is better for a person to fall sick in bed for twelve months,
than to have this decree made against him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, רָאוּי לוֹ שֶׁיִּפּוֹל לַמִּטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from step 21, giving רבי יהושע's reason.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהושע was the one upset, because of the painful decree to break his יום הכפורים.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא asks permission and points to a word written three times
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא asks רבי יהושע if he may repeat something רבי יהושע himself taught him, and points out that the Torah writes אֹתָם three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: My teacher, may I say before you one thing you taught me? He said: Speak. He said: The Torah says 'אֹתָם' three times.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers the sadness from Step 22 by first pointing out that a certain word appears three times. This sets up the teaching in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He respectfully asks permission, since he is about to teach his own teacher. He presents it as רבי יהושע's own teaching, so it comforts rather than lectures. Here he only points to the repeated word; what it means comes next.

phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher, allow me
to say before you one thing
that you taught me.
He said to him: Speak.
He said to him: Look, it says
"them," "them," "them" — three times.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:2, 23:4, 23:37, all about declaring the festivals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבִּי, תַּרְשֵׁינִי לוֹמַר לְפָנֶיךָ דָּבָר אֶחָד שֶׁלִּמַּדְתַּנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא begins answering the sadness רבי יהושע expressed in Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah repeats the word אֹתָם three times about declaring the festivals.

steps.title: Read it as you: the court's declaration stands no matter what
steps.stepSummary: Each אֹתָם is read as אַתֶּם, 'you': the בית דין's ruling stands even if it was a mistake, on purpose, or because they were fooled.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'You' — even by mistake. 'You' — even on purpose. 'You' — even if fooled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא explains the three אֹתָם words. They show that whatever day the בית דין declares as ראש חודש counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since אֹתָם can be read as אַתֶּם, the Torah is saying the declaring is up to 'you,' the בית דין. Each of the three repeats covers a different case: a mistake, a choice made on purpose, and being fooled. So רבן גמליאל's ruling counts even if רבי יהושע thought it was wrong, and giving in is not a sin.

keyTerms.meaning: You (plural), the same letters as אֹתָם

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source for the rule that the בית דין's setting of the calendar is binding even when it does not match the actual new moon.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the Torah is praising a בית דין that gets the date wrong on purpose. The point is only that once they declare the day, it counts, and the people must follow it.

phrases.english: "You" — even if by mistake,
phrases.notes: אֹתָם is written without a ו, so the same letters can be read אַתֶּם, 'you.'

phrases.english: "You" — even on purpose,
"You" — even if misled.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אַתֶּם״ — אֲפִילּוּ שׁוֹגְגִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the three אֹתָם words from Step 23 teach.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן גמליאל's declaration of ראש חודש counts, so רבי יהושע may follow it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The three times אֹתָם appears in ויקרא 23, read as אַתֶּם.

steps.title: רבי יהושע is comforted
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע tells רבי עקיבא: You have comforted me, you have comforted me.
steps.simpleTranslation: In these words he said to him: Akiva, you have comforted me, you have comforted me.
steps.whatsHappening: The story with רבי עקיבא ends. רבי יהושע accepts the teaching and is no longer upset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 22 he said being sick for a year would be better than this decree. Now he sees that going along with the בית דין is what the Torah wants, so his distress goes away. He says 'you have comforted me' twice to show how strongly he felt it.
steps.whatToRemember: The בית דין's declaration of the date counts no matter what (אַתֶּם, אַתֶּם, אַתֶּם), and this is what calmed רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: In these words he said to him:
Akiva, you have comforted me, you have comforted me.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּלָּשׁוֹן הַזֶּה אָמַר לוֹ: עֲקִיבָא נִחַמְתַּנִי, נִחַמְתַּנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהושע reacts to the teaching in Step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהושע accepts that the בית דין's ruling counts and is comforted.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about רבי דוסא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: רבי יהושע went to רבי דוסא בן הורכינס.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came to רבי דוסא בן הורכינס, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה so it can discuss it. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי דוסא בן הורכינס taught that every בית דין has the same standing as the בית דין of משה. He learned this from the fact that the names of משה's elders are not written. The גמרא now brings a ברייתא to explain that point.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for 'and so on'; the rest of the line is assumed

phrases.aramaic: בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל רַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הוֹרְכִּינָס כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: He came to Rabbi Dosa ben Horkinas, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל רַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הוֹרְכִּינָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the part about רבי עקיבא, the גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the משנה about רבי יהושע going to רבי דוסא בן הורכינס.

steps.title: Why are the elders' names not written?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks why the Torah does not give the names of משה's seventy elders.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Why were the names of these elders not spelled out?
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא asks a question about the פסוק that mentions the seventy elders without naming them. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah names משה, אהרן, נדב and אביהוא, but then only says 'seventy of the elders of Israel.' The ברייתא wants to know why the rest stay unnamed. This is the same point רבי דוסא used in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Elders, here the seventy judges with משה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Why were not spelled out
the names of these elders?
phrases.notes: These are the seventy elders in שמות 24:9, who went up with משה and אהרן.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לָמָּה לֹא נִתְפָּרְשׁוּ שְׁמוֹתָם שֶׁל זְקֵנִים הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to explain the reasoning behind רבי דוסא's line in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the Torah leaves out the names of the seventy elders.

steps.title: So no one belittles the judges of his own time
steps.stepSummary: The names were left out so people would not compare their own judges to great figures and decide those judges do not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that a person should not say: Is so-and-so like משה and אהרן? Is so-and-so like נדב and אביהוא? Is so-and-so like אלדד and מידד?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. Without names, no one can claim his generation's judges are not as good as the ones in משה's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the elders were all named, people might compare a judge of their own time to famous people and say he falls short. Since most of the elders are unnamed, any judge could be on their level. That means every generation's בית דין has full authority, which is exactly what רבי יהושע needed to hear about רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Sons of אהרן, named in the פסוק
Two elders who prophesied in the camp

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the idea that the leaders of each generation must be respected like those of earlier generations.

phrases.english: So that a person should not say:
Is so-and-so like Moshe and Aharon?
Is so-and-so like Nadav and Avihu?
Is so-and-so like Eldad and Medad?

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמַר אָדָם: פְּלוֹנִי כְּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The names were left out so no one would treat his own generation's judges as less important than the earlier ones.

steps.title: Two verses where שמואל lists great and lesser leaders together
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings two פסוקים from שמואל: one about משה and אהרן, and one listing ירובעל, בדן, יפתח and שמואל side by side.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: 'שמואל said to the people: It is ה׳ Who made משה and אהרן.' And it says: 'ה׳ sent ירובעל and בדן and יפתח and שמואל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds proof from פסוקים that small leaders are put next to great ones. It shows that each was the leader of his own generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the same speech, שמואל mentions משה and אהרן and then lists less famous judges together with himself. Putting them all in one list teaches that a judge like יפתח had full authority in his time, just as שמואל did in his. This backs up the lesson that every בית דין counts.

steps.raayaObject: That lesser leaders have the same authority in their generation as great ones had in theirs.

steps.title: Who are ירובעל, בדן and יפתח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the names: ירובעל is גדעון, בדן is שמשון, and יפתח is simply יפתח.
steps.simpleTranslation: ירובעל is גדעון, called that because he fought with the בעל. בדן is שמשון, called that because he came from דן. יפתח means just what it says.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the unusual names in the פסוק so we know which judges שמואל meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירובעל is a nickname for גדעון that comes from his fight against the idol בעל. בדן is a nickname for שמשון, meaning 'the one from דן.' יפתח needs no explanation because it is his real name.

keyTerms.meaning: The judge who was called ירובעל
The judge from the tribe of דן
As it sounds, the plain meaning

steps.whatToRemember: Every generation's leaders, even ones who seem small like יפתח, have full authority in their time. That is why רבי יהושע had to accept רבן גמליאל's ruling.

phrases.english: "Yerubaal" — this is Gidon,
and why is he called Yerubaal?
Because he made a fight with the Baal.
phrases.notes: The name sounds like 'let בעל fight,' from רִיב (fight) and בַּעַל.

phrases.english: "Bedan" — this is Shimshon,
and why is he called Bedan?
Because he came from Dan.
Yiftach — as it sounds.
